lesson.title: The Cooking Show: Teach Your Dish to the Class
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: This is where the week lands. You have a recipe card for a dish your family makes. Today you teach it — the way a chef on a cooking show teaches a dish: talk through the ingredients, walk the steps in order, and give the one thing a recipe card cannot, which is where the dish comes from and why it matters. Two to three minutes, in Spanish, from your card.

A cooking-show segment has a shape. Use these Spanish frames:
— Open: "Hoy les voy a enseñar a preparar..." (Today I'm going to teach you to make...) "Este plato es de... / En mi familia lo hace..." (This dish is from... / In my family it's made by...)
— Ingredients: "Necesitan estos ingredientes:..." (You need these ingredients:...) — hold up or point to each.
— Steps: "Primero... Luego... Después... Por último..." — one action per sentence, in order, present tense or commands.
— Taste: "El sabor es..." (dulce, salado, ácido, picante).
— Close: "En mi familia lo comemos cuando..." (In my family we eat it when...) "¡Buen provecho!"
You may hold cards, but look up between steps — this is a demonstration, not a reading.

A weak cooking-show segment is just a list read aloud. A strong one does the week's move: it presents the dish (the product) and, in one or two sentences, what the dish reveals (the perspective). "Este plato viene de la costa, donde el pescado es del día" — geography. "Solo lo hacemos para el Año Nuevo" — occasion. "Mi bisabuela lo cocinaba igual" — continuity. You have been reading mole and ceviche and coconut rice this way all week; now do it out loud with your own dish, for an audience. That sentence is what turns a recipe into a piece of a culture.

That is the week: from four dishes on a map Monday, to a real recipe Tuesday, to five centuries of food history Wednesday, to your own kitchen today. File your recipe card in the year-long portfolio. Next week the tense changes: narrating a trip in the past — el pretérito — telling a completed story from start to finish.

items.prompt: Translate to Spanish: mole (the Mexican sauce)

objectives: Deliver a 2–3 minute cooking-show presentation in Spanish from the Day 4 recipe card: opening, ingredients, steps in order, taste, close
Use all eight of the week's vocabulary words accurately (el sabor, picante, la receta, el ingrediente, el mole, el ceviche, la empanada, la gastronomía)
Include one or two spoken sentences connecting the dish to a perspective it reveals, per standard WA-WL-2015.2.2
materialsNeeded: The completed recipe card from Day 4
Optional: the real ingredients or photos of them as props
An audience — a class, a co-op group, or one listener
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Warm up with the vocabulary translate activity to confirm all eight words are solid.
2. Read the el-formato block; have the student mark their recipe card with the frames (where the opening goes, where 'Primero' starts, where the taste line goes).
3. Do one quiet run-through with the student reading straight from the card, just for timing.
4. Read the practice-to-perspective block. Have the student write their one perspective sentence on a sticky note and place it in the segment (usually near the open or the close).
5. Second run-through: card in hand but eyes up between steps. Coach for one action per sentence and clear sequence words.
6. Deliver the presentation to the audience.
7. Give the graded quiz (quiz-spanish-9-6-5) after the presentations.
8. File the recipe card in the year-long portfolio; preview next week's preterite / trip-narration unit.
differentiationTips: Struggling: a 90-second version with just open, three steps, and the perspective sentence is a full pass; let the student keep the card visible throughout
Ready for more: present with no card, add follow-up questions from the audience answered in Spanish, and use the tú or usted command register for the steps rather than the present tense
If there is no group, the presentation works delivered to one listener (a family member, a co-op parent) or recorded; the rubric does not change
teacherGuide.answerKey: There is no single correct presentation. Evaluate for: (1) the five-part shape — open, ingredients, ordered steps, taste, close; (2) steps genuinely in order, one action per sentence; (3) accurate use of all eight week-6 words; (4) at least one spoken sentence linking the dish to a perspective (geography, occasion, care, continuity); (5) delivered as a demonstration — eyes up between steps — not read start to finish. The graded quiz then checks dish-origin facts and the week's vocabulary.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Closes the week's WA-WL-2015.2.2 arc in the presentational mode: the student presents a cultural product (their dish) and states the perspective it reveals, for an audience. Per the scope-and-sequence's week 6 Day 5 design ('Cooking-show presentations — teach your dish to the class in Spanish'). The vocabulary translate recap confirms all eight words before the final task and before the graded quiz — the same closing pattern weeks 2, 4, and 5 use. The recipe card joins the year-long portfolio.
